title: "Not four strings but five: Brittany Haas"

I just love the sound of strings - I've been listening to the new album of Brittany Haas, an American violinist/fiddle player (who at one time [studied Evolutionary Biology at Princeton](https://www.brittanyhaas.com/biopress)! Hello fellow biologist with a love for music!).

Her latest album is the second one with her sister Natalie, who plays the cello. I find it amazing what variety of sounds these two can create!

<iframe style="border: 0; width: 100%; height: 120px;" src="https://bandcamp.com/EmbeddedPlayer/album=571412498/size=large/bgcol=ffffff/linkcol=0687f5/tracklist=false/artwork=small/transparent=true/" seamless><a href="https://brittanyhaas.bandcamp.com/album/north-node">North Node by Natalie &amp; Brittany Haas</a></iframe>

Brittany plays a five-string fiddle, so basically a combination of a violin and a viola. I've never played an acoustic one, only electric ones. I'd love to try one at some point! I think it makes her role in the duo much more versatile.

If you like strings but prefer (some of them) plucked, maybe this one is more for you: an album of her band Hawktail

<iframe style="border: 0; width: 100%; height: 120px;" src="https://bandcamp.com/EmbeddedPlayer/album=752691865/size=large/bgcol=ffffff/linkcol=0687f5/tracklist=false/artwork=small/transparent=true/" seamless><a href="https://hawktail.bandcamp.com/album/formations">Formations by Hawktail</a></iframe>

And recently she joined the Punch Brothers!

<iframe style="border: 0; width: 100%; height: 120px;" src="https://bandcamp.com/EmbeddedPlayer/album=361838896/size=large/bgcol=ffffff/linkcol=0687f5/tracklist=false/artwork=small/transparent=true/" seamless><a href="https://punchbrothers.bandcamp.com/album/the-unsung-adventures-of-punch-brothers">The Unsung Adventures of Punch Brothers by Punch Brothers</a></iframe>

The first album is still my favourite. Which one is yours?
